specimen.title: Sawa type specimen
specimen.lede: Sawa is a bilingual Arabic and English type family in serif, sans and mono, where both scripts share one set of proportions and vertical metrics, so a mixed line never changes height.
specimen.axis: {family}: weight axis {min, number} to {max, number}, default {def, number}.
lineHeight.intro: The same paragraph twice. In Sawa, Arabic and Latin share one line box, so every line is the same height. The second copy uses Source Sans 3, which has no Arabic, so your system substitutes its own Arabic font and the lines holding Arabic can grow taller.
lineHeight.gridNote: Bands mark each line box and a rule marks each baseline, computed from the family's own ascender, descender and units per em.
lineHeight.box: Line box {value} em: ascender {ascender, number}, descender {descender, number}, {upm, number} units per em.
lineHeight.statusNote: Source Sans 3 for Latin; the Arabic is whatever font your system picks.
tashkeel.intro: Al-Fatiha in Sawa Serif, fully vowelled, exactly as published by the Tanzil Project.

tashkeel.legendIntro: Sawa sorts its marks into groups so that each can get its own colour: vowels, tanween, sukun and the Quranic signs stay easy to tell apart.
tashkeel.noPalettes: {family} has no colour palettes yet, so the text above is set in a single colour. The legend shows the planned grouping.
families.intro: Three families with one set of proportions. Each is a variable font on a single weight axis.

about.title: About Sawa
about.body: Sawa (سوا), meaning "together" in Arabic, is a bilingual type family released under the SIL Open Font License. Sawa Serif and Sawa Sans are built from Noto Naskh Arabic, Noto Sans Arabic, Noto Serif and Noto Sans; Sawa Mono is built from Cascadia Mono. All of them are under the same licence.
